section_summary: This section contains documentation from early 1948 regarding economic conditions, fiscal policy, and political developments in occupied Japan. It opens with an extensive economic report analyzing industrial wages, inflation, tax collection failures, and government budget deficits, followed by State Department communications authorizing policy discussions on Japanese economic rehabilitation. The remaining documents consist of diplomatic despatches, memoranda of conversation, and correspondence concerning Japanese political instability, civil service and labor reforms, communist labor agitation, and proposals for American economic aid to achieve self-support.

subfiles.about: An economic study analyzing wage trends, producer and wholesale price inflation, budget deficits, and personal income tax collection failures in occupied Japan during fiscal year 1947-1948.
subfiles.summary: This report reviews Japanese economic trends, focusing on industrial wage increases, surging wholesale prices, and government price subsidies to basic industries. It details the severe failure of the revenue collection system in fiscal year 1947-1948, where personal income tax collections from self-assessed taxpayers lagged dramatically behind targets despite withholding success. The report also examines the rapid expansion of Bank of Japan note issue, attributing monetary inflation primarily to government budget deficits and Reconstruction Finance Bank lending.
subfiles.title: Report on Japanese Economic Conditions and Fiscal Policy (Wages, Prices, and Government Finances)

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Marshall authorizes George F. Kennan to discuss economic aspects of Japanese occupation policy with General Draper and his mission.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Marshall informs Acting POLAD for Kennan that, following talks with Secretary Royall, Kennan is authorized to discuss economic aspects of Japanese occupation policy with General Draper.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 116 to POLAD Tokyo Authorizing Economic Policy Discussions
subfiles.to: Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo (for George F. Kennan)

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Dr. Kurusu Takeo and Watanabe Yoshio concerning U.S. aid, the political stability of the Ashida Cabinet, exchange rates, civil service reform, and communist-led strikes.
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits a memorandum of a March 11, 1948 conversation with Economic Stabilization Board Director-General Kurusu Takeo and Finance Ministry Liaison Chief Watanabe Yoshio. Kurusu emphasized the importance of U.S. aid for Japan and the Philippines as bulwarks against communism, discussed political vulnerabilities facing the newly formed Ashida Cabinet, doubted the immediate feasibility of a single exchange rate, and criticized civil service reform demands. Also enclosed is a translated Yomiuri Shimbun article detailing communist-led Sanbetsu strike tactics intended to force general elections.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 178: Conversation with Director-General of the Economic Stabilization Board

subfiles.about: Memorandum summarizing a conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto regarding Japanese civil service reforms, economic advisers to SCAP, labor reforms, the Economic Stabilization Board, and press censorship.
subfiles.summary: Marshall Green summarizes key points from a meeting with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto, highlighting bureaucratic entrenchment under civil service reform, SCAP's lack of competent economic advisers, excessive labor privileges, Wada's departure from the Economic Stabilization Board, and damaging press censorship.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto Regarding Despatch No. 187

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto discussing the durability of Occupation reforms, Japanese militarism, population growth, American economic aid, SCAP administration, bureaucracy, and press censorship.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a memorandum of conversation of March 17, 1948, between Dr. Tsuru Shigeto, Marshall Green, and W. Henry Lawrence, Jr. Dr. Tsuru assessed that industrial decentralization would outlast land and labor reforms, warned of enduring militaristic nationalism unless living standards rise, and advocated for population control. He further discussed his pending resignation from the Economic Stabilization Board, criticized SCAP's lack of trained economists, condemned civil service reforms that preserved the bureaucracy, and protested severe press censorship.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 187: Conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto, Deputy Director General of Economic Stabilization Board

subfiles.about: Duplicate control copy of Despatch No. 187 transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto on Occupation reforms, political developments, and economic administration.
subfiles.summary: This is a duplicate control copy of Despatch No. 187 and its enclosed memorandum of conversation of March 17, 1948, received by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. It details Dr. Tsuru Shigeto's perspectives on the long-term prospects of Occupation reforms, population growth, political instability surrounding the Katayama and Ashida cabinets, defects in civil service reform, and censorship of American literature.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 187: Conversation with Dr. Tsuru Shigeto, Deputy Director General of Economic Stabilization Board (Duplicate Control Copy)

subfiles.about: Airgram transmitting the text of an editorial from The Times of London evaluating the political challenges and communist labor threats facing Prime Minister Ashida's government.
subfiles.summary: London Embassy airgram transmitting a March 23, 1948 editorial from The Times analyzing challenges facing the Ashida Government, communist trade union influence, and the American economic mission to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-787: Times Editorial Comment on "Japanese Government on Trial"

subfiles.about: Letter acknowledging notification that the Department of the Army prepared a $275 million appropriation request for economic recovery in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.summary: Treasury Department letter acknowledging receipt of State Department notice regarding the Army's $275 million appropriation request for economic recovery in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Army Appropriation Request for Economic Recovery in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Bank of Japan Governor Ichimada Hisato regarding U.S. aid priority over China, economic internationalism, industrial rationalization, and political unity.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a memorandum of a March 18, 1948 conversation with Bank of Japan Governor Ichimada Hisato and senior bank officials. Ichimada welcomed the shift in American policy toward Japanese self-support, urged prioritizing aid to Japan over China, and proposed an Asian Marshall Plan to foster an economically unified world. He recommended discharging 2.5 million redundant workers to rationalize industry, attaining domestic political unity, securing substantial foreign credits, and introducing new revenues to curb currency inflation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 204: Conversation with Governor of the Bank of Japan
